L7: In Kansas, counties are responsible for solid waste planning, and in Johnson County this is done through the cite2†Johnson County Solid Waste Management Committee who develop a solid waste management plan (SWMP). The Board of County Commissioners formally adopts the SWMP after a required public hearing, and it is ultimately approved by the cite3†Kansas Department of Health and Environment†www.kdhe.ks.gov to become official.
L8:  As required by Kansas law, the plan is reviewed annually to track the completion of and progress towards short and long term goals that are called out in the SWMP.
L9: ## 2024 Solid Waste Management Plan
L10: 
L11: The board-appointed Johnson County Solid Waste Management Committee (SWMC) developed a cite4†Solid Waste Management Plan (SWMP) to guide how the community will manage solid waste in the county, per KSA 65-3405. The Johnson County Board of County Commissioners adopted this new plan on Sept. 5, 2024. The SWMP satisfies state regulatory requirements that require counties to develop a comprehensive update to the SWMP every five years.

L40: ## Solid Waste Management Code
L41: The purpose of the Solid Waste Management Code is to protect the public health, safety, and welfare of the residents of Johnson County. It provides uniform and prudent regulations of solid waste within the county, from its generation through its collection, storage, transportation, processing, treatment and disposal. The Code requires licenses and permits at the county level for the collection and transportation of solid waste, and for the operation of solid waste processing facilities.
L42: It also provides procedures for investigation and resolution of the improper disposal of solid waste in the unincorporated areas of Johnson County.
L43: cite6†Johnson County Code of Regulations for Solid Waste Management L44: ## Waste Characterization Study
L45: Every few years Environmental Division staff conduct a waste characterization study to see how the overall waste stream of Johnson County has changed. As with the 2006 study, three sites were selected within the county, including the cite7†Waste Management Landfill†www.wmsolutions.com , the cite8†City of Olathe Transfer Station†www.olatheks.gov , and the APAC-Reno Construction and Demolition Debris Landfill.
L46: Representative samples were taken from each location and analyzed to see what the Johnson County waste stream is comprised of, which then allows DHE staff to incorporate that information into future solid waste planning efforts.
